summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn opened with a childhood memory of his family's home being broken into, and how deeply it hurts to have something precious taken. He used that experience to illustrate John 10:10: the enemy is a thief who wants to steal our peace, joy, family, health, purpose, and ultimately our soul, while Jesus came to give life abundantly. Drawing on David's courage in 1 Samuel 17, Pastor Travis declared 2024 the "year of the take back" and called Impact Church to stop sitting passively and to go after, in faith, what God has promised.

He then shared four things to never do in 2024. First, never stop believing. Pointing to Matthew 19:26, Isaiah 43, and Romans 15:13, he encouraged the church to let go of the past, trust that all things are possible with God, and overflow with hope. Even mustard seed faith is enough, and faith grows by hearing God's Word (Romans 10:17), so we should be careful what we give our eyes and ears to. He shared honestly that his own family has walked through a hard season, and that 1 Peter 5:10 is the promise he clings to.

Second, never stop praying. Prayer should be our first choice, not our last resort. Using Romans 12:12, James 5, and Jonah's prayer from inside the fish, he reminded us that we can pray from any place in life. He then walked through King Jehoshaphat in 2 Chronicles 20, who faced overwhelming odds, sought the Lord, and proclaimed a fast. Pastor Travis announced a 21-day church fast beginning that day and ending January 27. He explained that a biblical fast sets aside something, such as food, social media, or television, and replaces it with prayer and Scripture. A QR code offered details and a daily devotional.

Third, never unplug from the body of Christ. Citing Hebrews 10:25, he taught that the enemy wants believers isolated, and that real connection comes through relationships, not just Sunday attendance. He shared how time spent serving at his church after a hard night at age 17 surrounded him with believers who shaped his life. He compared the church to redwood trees, whose shallow roots intertwine so that they stand together through storms.

Fourth, never stop praising. Using Isaiah 61, Jehoshaphat's singers who went ahead of the army, and Hebrews 13:15, he described a "sacrifice of praise": thanking God even when we do not feel like it. He invited anyone who had not yet trusted Christ to receive God's free gift of salvation, then closed in prayer and led the church to praise God anyway.
mainPoints: Never stop believing and hoping: God's promises are true, faith grows by hearing His Word, and even mustard seed faith is enough to hold on to Him.
Never stop praying and praising: like Jehoshaphat, turn to God first through prayer, fasting, and a sacrifice of praise, saying "we do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you."
Never unplug from the body of Christ: the enemy wants us isolated, but real connection through relationships with God's family brings strength, protection, and endurance.

versesMentioned.text: The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I came that they may have life and have it abundantly.

But David persisted. "I have been taking care of my father's sheep and goats," he said. "When a lion or a bear comes to steal a lamb from the flock, I go after it with a club and rescue the lamb from its mouth. If it turns on me, I catch it by the jaw and club it to death. I have done this to both lions and bears, and I'll do it to this pagan Philistine, too, for he has defied the armies of the living God!"
Jesus looked at them and said, "With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible."
Forget the former things; do not dwell on the past. See, I am doing a new thing! Now it springs up; do you not perceive it? I am making a way in the wilderness and streams in the wasteland.
May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you trust in him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
For what you have done I will always praise you in the presence of your faithful people. And I will hope in your name, for your name is good.

He replied, "Because you have so little faith. Truly I tell you, if you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you."
So then faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.
And the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory in Christ, after you have suffered a little while, will himself restore you and make you strong, firm and steadfast.
Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, faithful in prayer.

Is anyone among you in trouble? Let them pray. Is anyone happy? Let them sing songs of praise. Is anyone among you sick? Let them call the elders of the church to pray over them and anoint them with oil in the name of the Lord. And the prayer offered in faith will make the sick person well; the Lord will raise them up. If they have sinned, they will be forgiven. Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective.

From inside the fish Jonah prayed to the Lord his God. He said: "In my distress I called to the Lord, and he answered me. From deep in the realm of the dead I called for help, and you listened to my cry."

Alarmed, Jehoshaphat resolved to inquire of the Lord, and he proclaimed a fast for all Judah. The people of Judah came together to seek help from the Lord; indeed, they came from every town in Judah to seek him.
Jesus answered, "It is written: 'Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.'"

Lord, the God of our ancestors, are you not the God who is in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. Power and might are in your hand, and no one can withstand you. Our God, did you not drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel and give it forever to the descendants of Abraham your friend?
Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no power to face this vast army that is attacking us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you.

He said: "Listen, King Jehoshaphat and all who live in Judah and Jerusalem! This is what the Lord says to you: Do not be afraid or discouraged because of this vast army. For the battle is not yours, but God's."
not giving up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.

and provide for those who grieve in Zion: to bestow on them a crown of beauty instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, and a garment of praise instead of a spirit of despair. They will be called oaks of righteousness, a planting of the Lord for the display of his splendor.

After consulting the people, Jehoshaphat appointed men to sing to the Lord and to praise him for the splendor of his holiness as they went out at the head of the army, saying: "Give thanks to the Lord, for his love endures forever." As they began to sing and praise, the Lord set ambushes against the men of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir who were invading Judah, and they were defeated.
Through Jesus, therefore, let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that openly profess his name.
I will extol the Lord at all times; his praise will always be on my lips. I will glory in the Lord; let the afflicted hear and rejoice. Glorify the Lord with me; let us exalt his name together.

Monday.scripture: Matthew 19:26 (NIV): "With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible."
Monday.focus: Never stop believing: trusting that nothing is too hard for God.
Monday.action: Write down one situation that feels discouraging. Next to it, write "With God all things are possible," and put the note where you will see it throughout the day.
Monday.prayer: Father, You are a God of hope and miracles. Strengthen my belief today, and help me to trust You with the situation I have written down. In Jesus' name, amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Romans 10:17 (NKJV): "So then faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God."
Tuesday.focus: Feeding your faith by putting God's promises before your eyes and ears.
Tuesday.action: Choose one promise from Scripture (such as 1 Peter 5:10) and read it aloud in the morning and again at night. Limit one discouraging voice or input today, such as a news feed or social media scroll.
Tuesday.prayer: Lord, help me to be careful about what I give my eyes and ears to. Grow my faith as I hold on to Your Word and Your promises. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Romans 12:12 (NIV): "Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, faithful in prayer."
Wednesday.focus: Making prayer your first choice, not your last resort.
Wednesday.action: Before checking your phone this morning, spend ten quiet minutes talking with God about everything on your heart. Each time you feel worried today, stop and pray right then.
Wednesday.prayer: God, thank You that I can come to You at any time and in any place. Teach me to turn to You first and to stay faithful in prayer. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: 2 Chronicles 20:12 (NIV): "We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you."
Thursday.focus: Seeking God through prayer and fasting with your eyes fixed on Him.
Thursday.action: Join the church fast by choosing one thing to set aside today, such as social media or television, and use that time to pray and read Scripture. If you choose to fast from food, do so only if you are healthy, and talk with your doctor first if you have any concerns.
Thursday.prayer: Lord, I do not always know what to do, but my eyes are on You. Draw me closer to You as I seek You, and help me to hunger for You more than anything else. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Hebrews 10:25 (NIV): "not giving up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another."
Friday.focus: Staying connected to the body of Christ through real relationships.
Friday.action: Reach out to one person from your church family with an encouraging message, a phone call, or an invitation to coffee. If you are not yet in a group or serving team, look up one way to get connected.
Friday.prayer: Father, thank You for the family of God. Keep me from isolation, and help me to encourage others and to be strengthened by them. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Hebrews 13:15 (NIV): "Through Jesus, therefore, let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that openly profess his name."
Saturday.focus: Offering God praise anyway, even when we do not feel like it.
Saturday.action: Play or sing a worship song out loud and name three things you can thank God for today, including one in a hard area of your life. Then prepare your heart to worship together with your church family.
Saturday.prayer: Lord, I praise You because You are good and Your love endures forever. Even on days when it is hard, I choose to lift up Your name. Amen.

title: Taking Back What’s Mine
speaker: Pastor Travis Hearn
